messages:
jamal: Hey team — customer hit a sudden NXDOMAIN for their service endpoint (svc.acme.internal) from a tenant VPC after a resolver policy push. Works from our prod VPC. Can we triage?

maria: Which customer + any recent infra changes?

jamal: acme-inc. They just applied a resolver policy change (pinned forwarder for .internal -> shared-resolver) about ~30m ago. I can repro from their bastion.

maria: Can you paste dig +trace and output from the bastion? Also include iptables/nat egress info if possible.

jamal: Pasting minimal repro:

```
$ dig svc.acme.internal +short

;; -> no output (NXDOMAIN)

$ dig svc.acme.internal @169.254.169.253 +short

;; -> NXDOMAIN

$ dig +trace svc.acme.internal
;; global options: +cmd
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```

jamal: curl to the service endpoint IP (when we manually resolve via their internal DNS in a different VPC) times out. From our prod VPC the same name resolves to 10.2.5.14. From their tenant VPC NXDOMAIN.

sasha: Two high-prob causes: 1) split-horizon/private hosted zone shadowing (another private hosted zone with same name in a different account/VPC), 2) resolver rule routing/stub-domain mis-route. Did they recently associate any hosted zones or modify cross-account associations?

jamal: They did request a cross-account assoc last week but we denied it. However their infra team did a policy change to route .internal to the org-shared-resolver (account 999). That coincides with the break.

alex: Can we confirm whether a private hosted zone for acme.internal exists in the shared-resolver account and whether that hosted zone is associated to the tenant VPC? If a hosted zone exists in shared account but not associated to tenant VPC, and the tenant now forwards to the shared resolver, queries might hit a resolver without the zone => NXDOMAIN.

jamal: Good call — digging now.

aws-bot: (automated) Note: Route53 hosted zone change detected in account 999 at 2026-03-17T08:45:12Z — private hosted zone "acme.internal" created.

maria: If the forwarded resolver hosts a private zone for acme.internal but it's not associated to the tenant VPC, forwarded queries won't find records. Also check resolver rule priority: if there's a VPC-local resolver rule or node-local cache, it could be shadowing.

jamal: Found hosted zones: account 111 (customer) has private zone acme.internal associated to their VPC. account 999 (shared-resolver) also has a private zone acme.internal but NOT associated to customer VPC. The resolver forwarder was set to account 999.

sasha: Yep that's the split-horizon shadowing case. Forwarding queries to account 999 resolver that has a zone by the same name but not associated to their VPC leads to NXDOMAIN. The correct pattern is either: A) forward to resolver that HAS the zone associated to the VPC, or B) remove the duplicate zone from the shared account.

alex: Short-term mitigation: revert the resolver policy so tenant VPC uses system resolver (node-local) or a forwarder that has the zone associated. Or associate the shared account hosted zone to the tenant VPC (but that may have cross-account permission implications).

jamal: Reverting policy now for customer (rolling back to previous resolver IP). Will report back.

eng-sre: Please capture the following for root cause: - which resolver rule was applied (rule-id), - which hosted zones exist for acme.internal across accounts, - VPC associations for each zone, - recent IAM events for CreateHostedZone/AssociateVPC. We'll need to coordinate cross-account zoning policy.

maria: Also check security group / NACL egress allowlists — forwarding traffic to the shared resolver requires UDP/53 and TCP/53 outbound allowed. If that was blocked, we might see timeouts rather than NXDOMAIN, but worth verifying.

jamal: Rollback successful — svc.acme.internal resolves again from tenant bastion. Customer confirms API calls are green.

sasha: Root cause summary (tentative): resolver policy change forwarded .internal to shared-resolver account 999 which contains a duplicate private hosted zone "acme.internal" that is NOT associated with the tenant VPC. Forwarded queries therefore returned NXDOMAIN.

alex: Remediation options:
- Remove duplicate private hosted zone in shared account or rename to avoid shadowing.
- If shared resolver must hold a zone, associate that private hosted zone with the tenant VPC (cross-account associate) and ensure permissions are approved.
- Add a resolver rule with explicit target that points to the customer-owned resolver that has the zone associated.
- Add automation checks to detect duplicate private hosted zones (same zone name across accounts) and warn on resolver policy changes.

maria: I'll follow up with the customer and coordinate next steps (change control for cross-account association or rollback of org-level resolver policy). I opened an internal ticket: #SUP-4821.

jamal: Thanks everyone. Leaving ticket with eng-sre + infra for cross-account cleanup. :raised_hands:

eng-sre: Noted — will escalate to infra governance for policy/automation.

aws-bot: (automated) Reminder: when changing resolver policies, run the 'hz-check' script to detect hosted zone name collisions: https://runbooks.internal/hz-check
